Particle Painting

Drag to stir · tap to shatter

Picture

Your image stays in this browser; it isn’t uploaded anywhere. Ink on paper flips the idea: dots land where the picture is dark.

How it’s sampled

1 · Read each pixel’s brightness L. 2 · Stretch the picture’s range so its darkest 2% is 0 and brightest 0.5% is 1. 3 · Raise to the power γ (Contrast) and add a little Fill: that is each pixel’s chance of getting a dot. 4 · Throw the dots: pick a random number, find which pixel it falls in on the running total (a binary search). Bright areas collect many dots. Each dot keeps only its pixel’s hue — brightness comes from how crowded the dots are.

Dots

Fewer, bigger dots read as pointillism; many small ones read as a photo. Contrast 1 = dots follow brightness exactly; higher pushes them into the highlights and leaves the shadows empty. Trails = how much of the last frame stays: smooth paint when still, streaks when moving.

Motion

Stir: your finger drags nearby dots along with it, and they drift back home. Shatter: how far the dots fly when you tap; near the tap they go first and farthest. Morph = how long they take to gather into the next picture. Focus 0 leaves them scattered.
